key_gap: vs baseline: both sides produce the identical correct explanation (heat-mover loop: refrigerant boils inside absorbing heat, compressor squeezes it hot, back coils condense it releasing heat to the room; pump does work; insulation slows the leak) and both name the same gap ('the fridge makes cold' treats cold as a substance; the child's 'where does the cold come from?' cuts the story at 'makes'). The v5 AI loss was timing and instrument: it reached the break only after generating and rejecting alternatives in HOW, while the human used the child's question as a first-pass scalpel on the naive sentence ('cold isn't a thing to add, it's a leak to fight'). The v6 routed run closes it: the m028 assumption-break pass breaks Priya's own sentence as the FIRST move (cold-as-substance assumption -> heat-mover), the m044 stakeholder pass finds the hidden requirement (a one-line truth so sales cannot revert to 'makes cold'), and m084 reads the stall as a free-rider tell (everyone profits from the shared shallow story; nobody owns the gap). The break is now first-class instead of post-hoc, at a small efficiency cost (dual-route + packet vs the human's single pure pass).
learning_signal: On explanation tasks the diagnostic instrument is the naive sentence in the user's own words, and the routed assumption-break pass (m028) is the correct first-class move: enumerate the assumptions the on-table claim makes ('cold is a substance the fridge produces'), break the load-bearing one, and the breakdown point IS the learning target — name it precisely (cold = absence of heat; the fridge moves heat out, it does not manufacture cold) before any alternative generation. The child-level questions ('where does the cold come from?', 'why is the back warm?', 'why doesn't it leak back?') are the acceptance test, and the oversimplification guard is the re-explanation's completion contract: plain words must carry the mechanism (evaporation absorbs, compression heats, condensation releases, insulation slows), never a cold-as-substance phrasing. Stakeholder and coordination passes add the non-reasoning half of the win: the one-line truth is the deliverable that stops a sales team free-riding on the shallow story.
suggested_improvement: Make the naive-claim assumption-break a standing first move of the m028 pass for explanation/understanding tasks (contract: enumerate assumptions of the on-table claim, break the load-bearing one, name the gap as the learning target, re-explain and accept the user's own questions); require the decision packet to contain the one-line plain truth (m044 hidden-requirement output) and the acceptance-test questions as verification evidence; keep the dual-route (m028+m044, m084 context) on simple-concept/high-stakes-signature explanation cases where routing confidence is low.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline executed its signature move and it backfired — it wrote the simple story ('just add more retries — computers are fast, extra requests are nothing'), read it back through the child's question ('doesn't that make it MORE struggling?'), smoothed the objection over ('it's busy, not broken'), and declared the explanation complete because it explained simply, validating elegance instead of truth (approving Dana's rule). The v5 AI already won this on the three-fact check (saturation = amplification, non-idempotent = double-settle, rising timeouts = persistent). The v6 routed run hardens the win: the m028 pass breaks 'retries are free' as the first move and lands the honest one-liner ('Trying again is also work — and some tries can't be undone'); m018's steelman shows Dana's rule fails in its strongest form; m019's vectors quantify double-settle, herd, and retry-storm; and the mandatory m003 (6 ranked failure categories incl. double-settle, un-mitigable residual named) and m007 (blanket retries ruin-adjacent with a one-shot double-charge branch; floor = retry less, telemetry-anchored) gates convert the rejection into a priced decision.
learning_signal: The Feynman failure mode is validating explanatory elegance instead of correctness — the method checks 'can I explain it simply?' and has no step that checks 'is the simple explanation true against the actual system?' — and the v6 routing answer is the oversimplification guard as a deliverable contract: on 'simple-answer' cases the routed assumption-break (m028: break 'retries are free' -> trying again is work, some tries can't be undone) supplies the honest simple sentence, and the mandatory protective gates (m003 on g:guarantee, m007 on c:high_stakes) force every clause of the simplified rule to survive the operative constraints (saturation = amplification, non-idempotent = irreversible, rising timeouts = persistent, not transient). A simplified answer is safe only where the load-bearing complexity is named in plain words and kept — 'what the simple version erases' must be an explicit line, and comprehension of a child is the acceptance test only when the constraint check has already passed.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m028/m018/m019 routing with m003+m007 gates on high_stakes guarantee signatures (trap-avoided; negative split held, T3 protected); add 'what the simple version erases' as a mandatory decision-packet line (rule 36-style completion contract: the load-bearing complexity named in plain words — here: each retry is new work on an overloaded machine and some retries are irreversible); extend the m028 pass contract with the flip move (under saturation retry LESS, not more) for capacity-symptom signatures, and record the retries-as-commons insight (herd = tragedy of the commons with a machine; the shared protocol is the institution) as a standing m019 baseline-risk check.
